original_value: This paper reviews automated visual-based defect detection approaches applicable to various materials, such as metals, ceramics and textiles. In the first part of the paper, we present a general taxonomy of the different defects that fall in two classes: visible (e.g., scratches, shape error, etc.) and palpable (e.g., crack, bump, etc.) defects. Then, we describe artificial visual processing techniques that are aimed at understanding of the captured scenery in a mathematical/logical way. We continue with a survey of textural defect detection based on statistical, structural and other approaches. Finally, we report the state of the art for approaching the detection and classification of defects through supervised and non-supervised classifiers and deep learning.

result.paraphrase: This paper surveys automated visual defect detection methods for a range of materials, including metals, ceramics, and textiles. In the opening section, we provide a general taxonomy of defect types split into two categories: visible defects such as scratches and shape errors, and palpable defects such as cracks and bumps. We then discuss artificial visual processing techniques intended to interpret captured scenes in mathematical and logical terms. Next, we review texture-based defect detection using statistical, structural, and related methods. Finally, we summarize the state of the art in detecting and classifying defects with supervised and unsupervised classifiers as well as deep learning.
